title: Tickets sell out and draw crowds in BH this weekend
seoTitle: Tickets sell out and attract crowds in BH this weekend
subtitle: Music, theater and food programming drives ticket sales in the Minas Gerais capital
excerpt: A variety of cultural events arrive in Belo Horizonte this weekend, sparking high demand for both paid and free tickets and energizing the scene.
author: Daniele Morais
sourceName: G1, Correio Braziliense, Estado de Minas
contentHtml:
The weekend of September 19‑21 brings a packed agenda of concerts, operas, parties and free shows in Belo Horizonte and the surrounding area, which explains the surge in ticket searches. The range of options – from tours by major music stars to craft‑beer festivals – means the public needs to know how to purchase or pick up their tickets.

Ivete Clareou: online ticket purchase

Singer Ivete Sangalo returns to the capital with the “Ivete Clareou” tour on Saturday, the 19th, at the outdoor area of Mineirinho. The show, featuring Liniker and the group Akatu as guests, includes a 360º stage, a food court, hydration stations and welcome spaces. Tickets are sold through a link provided in the cultural agenda.

Fafá de Belém: free ticket with pick‑up

The musical celebrating Fafá de Belém’s 70th birthday and 50 years of career will be performed on September 18 and 19 at 8 p.m. at Sesc Palladium. Admission is free, but attendees must collect their tickets at the designated points before the performance date.

Filomena: 32 Years of Struggle – free ticket with pick‑up

Gorete Milagres presents the show “Filomena: 32 Years of Struggle” at Teatro Feluma on September 19 and 20. The play is free and tickets must be obtained via a specific link. The same rule applies to the workshop “From Creation to Character Humanization,” offered on Sunday, the 20th, also at Teatro Feluma.

Contagem Beer Festival: ticket combo

The free event that gathers craft breweries, bar‑style food and rock shows takes place on Saturday, the 19th, at Praça Presidente Tancredo Neves in Contagem. Although entry is free, visitors can purchase beverage and food combos by buying tickets available through the indicated link.

Chica da Silva Opera: paid ticket

The opera “Chica da Silva,” produced by the Clóvis Salgado Foundation, will be staged at the Grand Teatro Cemig, Palácio das Artes, on September 19, 21 and 23. The production features an orchestra, choir and dance company, with about 163 artists on stage. Tickets are sold through the venue’s official channels.

Quarteirão das Artes and Festival Acessa BH: free ticket with pick‑up

From September 17 to 19, Quarteirão das Artes offers music, theater, dance, visual arts and a creative fair at various city locations. Admission is free, but tickets must be collected via the provided link. Festival Acessa BH, occurring on the 17th, 18th and 19th, follows the same free pick‑up model for its theater, performance and circus shows.

With so many options, the demand for tickets – whether for online purchase or in‑person pick‑up – reflects the enthusiasm of Belo Horizonte’s public for culture and leisure this weekend.

Information from G1, Correio Braziliense, Estado de Minas.
